text: That evening: Holmes says the bed was clamped to the floor
why: At ¶214 Holmes makes the remark in the gathering darkness at the Crown Inn, the same evening as the story's events.

text: Why was the bed in the middle room clamped to the floor?
why: A plain question the story has just raised by having Holmes single out the clamped bed.

text: Why was the bed in the middle room clamped to the floor? — a practical reason of the household, with no bearing on the case
id: q.why_bed_clamped=a practical reason of the household, with no bearing on the case
why: Asserts the clamping has no bearing on the case, which the story does not establish and which Holmes's framing (¶208-214) cuts against.

text: Who had the bed clamped to the floor?
why: A plain question about who clamped the bed; the story has not answered it, and the reader has reason to ask.

text: Who had the bed clamped to the floor? — an earlier occupant, for some forgotten reason
id: q.who_clamped=an earlier occupant, for some forgotten reason
why: Suggests an earlier occupant with a forgotten reason; nothing in the story so far mentions earlier occupants or such a reason.

text: When was the bed clamped to the floor?
why: A plain question about when the bed was clamped, which the story has not answered.

text: When was the bed clamped to the floor? — about the time the ventilator and the rope were put in
id: q.when_clamped=about the time the ventilator and the rope were put in
why: The story says the ventilator and bell-rope were added at about the same time (¶154-156), so this timing is a possibility the reader has reason to consider.

text: When was the bed clamped to the floor? — long before those changes
why: The story describes the room as old and gives no date for the bed, so a date long before the changes is an open possibility.

text: How could anything have reached Julia in a room shut on every side? — a rope runs from just above the opening to the pillow, on a bed that cannot be moved
why: The story states the bell-rope hangs by the bed with its tassel on the pillow, fastened above the ventilator opening (¶142, 151), and that the bed is clamped (¶214); the room is said to be sealed (¶56, ¶87).
